en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Itthivimāna (The Mansions of Women)
8. The Story of the Mango Mansion “Divine is your mango grove, delightful;
here stands a great palace.”
Resounding with the music of various instruments and filled with the voices of throngs of celestial nymphs,
a lamp burns here.
It was a great golden mountain,
perpetually surrounded on all sides by trees bearing garments as their fruit.
“By what means do you have such a complexion...
[as before] ...and your complexion illuminates all directions?”
That deity, being uplifted in mind...
[as before] ...this is the fruit of that karma.
“In a previous birth, when I was among humans in the human world,
I had a monastery built for the Saṅgha.”
Surrounded by women,
when the monastery was completed and the great festival had been performed.
Having covered it with cloths and having fashioned a cloth-wick,
she lit a lamp there.
Having fed that supreme assembly,
with my own hands and full of faith, I offered it to the Saṅgha.
Because of that, my mango grove is delightful,
and here is a large palace resounding with the music of various instruments.
Resounding with the cries of throngs of celestial nymphs,
a great golden lamp burns there perpetually.
Surrounded on all sides by trees bearing bitter fruit; because of that,
my complexion is such as this.
"...and my beauty shines forth in all directions.
Thus ends the eighth, the Mango Mansion.
